error.signature: AI tells a traveler to Kenya that plastic shopping bags are fine to carry or use, the same as in most countries

verdict.summary: Kenya banned the use, manufacture, and import of plastic carrier bags nationwide in 2017 under Legal Notice No. 2356 (Environmental Management and Co-ordination Act). Merely carrying one - including a duty-free or hotel giveaway bag - risks on-the-spot confiscation and, on paper, a fine of up to KES 4 million (~$40,000) or up to four years' imprisonment. Exemptions are narrow: garbage bin liners, medical-waste packaging, construction packaging, and primary industrial packaging.

dead_ends.action: Assume plastic shopping/grocery bags are unremarkable to bring into or use in Kenya, as in most countries
dead_ends.why_fails: Kenya's ban covers the use, manufacture, and import of flat plastic carrier bags for commercial and household packaging nationwide, with penalties of up to KES 4 million or four years in prison on the statute books. Customs officers at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport and other ports of entry are known to confiscate plastic bags on sight, including ones picked up during a duty-free layover purchase, even though full prosecution of tourists is rare in practice.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Travelers often assume the fine is purely theoretical and never enforced against visitors; in practice bags are still commonly confiscated at entry points even when prosecution is rare.

dead_ends.action: Assume only large branded shopping bags are banned, so small produce bags, ziplock-style packing bags, or bin liners are equally restricted
dead_ends.why_fails: The exemptions are narrow and specific: garbage bin liners, medical-waste packaging, construction packaging, and primary industrial packaging. Flat plastic carrier bags used for retail or household packaging are banned regardless of size, and there is no blanket exemption for 'small' bags.

workarounds.action: Pack a reusable cloth or jute tote for shopping in Kenya, and use your daypack or hand luggage instead of any plastic bag received during a layover.

If you do arrive holding a plastic bag, expect it may be confiscated at customs without argument - transfer any valuables or fragile items to hand luggage before landing rather than leaving them in the bag.
